author: Declaration Desk
title: Howrah's new ward map challenged in High Court, adding doubt to December civic polls
dek: A CPI(M) leader has asked the Calcutta High Court to set aside the redrawing of Howrah's wards from 50 to 68, a week after the court halted Kolkata's poll over a similar challenge.
body:
The redrawing of Howrah's municipal wards has been challenged in the Calcutta High Court, putting a second question mark over the civic elections the state government wants to hold in Kolkata and Howrah in December. The petition was admitted on Friday and is likely to be heard on 17 November, according to reports.

It was filed by Imtiaz Ahmed, a CPI(M) leader from Howrah and a former member of the Howrah Municipal Corporation's mayor-in-council, and is before a single-judge vacation bench of Justice Hiranmay Bhattacharya, reports said.

## What is being challenged

In August the Assembly passed amendments to the laws governing both corporations, raising the number of wards in Howrah from 50 to 68 and in Kolkata from 144 to 209. Introducing the bills, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that after the increase "the State Election Commission will determine the boundaries of the wards, the number of voters, population and other details". The Municipal Affairs Minister, Agnimitra Paul, said the decision had been taken "because of variations in population".

Opposition parties have objected to the formula used to draw the new boundaries and alleged irregularities in the process, according to reports. The specific grounds of Mr Ahmed's petition have not been reported. The CPI(M) is so far the only party to have taken the delimitation to court, one report said.

## Kolkata's poll already on hold

The Howrah case follows a similar challenge to Kolkata's new map filed by Dipu Das, a former CPI(M) councillor. On 6 November a Division Bench of Justices Sabyasachi Bhattacharyya and Arjun Ray Mukherjee barred the State Election Commission from notifying the Kolkata Municipal Corporation election until a single judge decides that case. Both corporations had been expected to vote in December, with results in January.

Kolkata has had no elected council since its board was dissolved in June. Howrah has been without one for far longer: its elected board's term ended in 2018, and it has since been run by officials appointed by the government.

## What each side says

Mr Adhikari has said the state will go to the Supreme Court against the order on Kolkata, though no petition had been reported as filed by Friday. On Thursday he said that if elections to the two corporations could not be held by 1 December, his government would appoint ward coordinators who "stand by the government". The BJP's state president, Samik Bhattacharya, has backed him.

Opposition parties accuse the government of redrawing wards to its own advantage and of planning to run the corporations through party loyalists. Mr Adhikari has accused them of using the courts to delay a vote they expect to lose.

## What happens next

- 17 November: the Howrah petition is likely to be heard by the vacation bench.
- The Kolkata delimitation case is pending before a single judge; no hearing date has been reported.
- 1 December: Mr Adhikari's deadline for appointing ward coordinators if polls cannot be held.
